title: Cape Canaveral Space Force Museum
specs: Displays numerous missiles, rockets, and related space flight equipment and memorabilia
Museum grounds encompass two adjoining launch complexes, Launch Complex 26 and Launch Complex 5/6
Highlights the Space Force as a major participant in America’s space program
Only individuals with active CCSFS installation privileges may access the station; military ID alone does not grant access
Off-station and on-station facilities available as event spaces for military and aerospace-related groups
includes: Docents at each site to guide and answer questions during open hours
Wheelchairs for visitors to borrow free of charge at each facility
gap: Price for commercial tours not stated
blurb: The museum displays numerous missiles, rockets, and related space flight equipment and memorabilia at several buildings and nearby facilities including Launch Complex 26 and Launch Complex 5/6. It highlights the Space Force's role in America's space program and activities at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station from the early 1950s to today. The museum opened in 1966 and is managed by the Museum Director, a civilian employee of Space Launch Delta 45.
extraNote: Admission and parking are free · No formal tours offered by museum; commercial tours available for a charge · Enclosed drinks allowed; food and open drinks not allowed inside without prior authorization · Only service animals allowed within museum/history center · No lockers or storage facilities available · 191 Museum Circle, Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, FL 32925
